observation.visible_scene: A single white twin‑engine commercial jet, marked with a red/pink tail logo and red wingtip accents, viewed from below against a cloudless, uniform blue sky. The aircraft is the only object in frame and stays roughly center‑right throughout.
visible_changes: The plane drifts slowly toward the left and slightly upward across the frame from the first to the last view.
Its apparent size remains nearly constant, so its distance from the viewpoint does not change much during the excerpt.

The fuselage attitude rotates gradually: early frames show a steep diagonal (nose upper‑left, tail lower‑right), while later frames show a shallower, more horizontal orientation (nose left, tail right).

Correspondingly the wing span tilts and the belly/underside of the aircraft becomes more visible toward the end, consistent with a slow bank/roll or a change in viewing angle rather than an abrupt maneuver.
The red tail marking and red wingtip highlights persist continuously; no editing cut or scene change occurs inside the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the leftward drift and rotation continue, reverse, or level off beyond the crop boundaries.
The aircraft's true heading, speed, altitude, and flight phase.
Whether the camera is panning/tracking or stationary, since the featureless sky gives no background reference.
uncertain_details: The exact bank or roll angle of the aircraft.
Whether the apparent motion is the plane's own translation or camera movement (indistinguishable against the uniform sky).
Whether the change in orientation is roll, yaw, or a combination.
